judgements.justification: A's AC wrote 'all reviewers were negative' although nMFp's 6 was never edited, and omitted the BDD100K test and KITTI-MOTS results the rebuttal supplied, toward A's reject.
No reviewer or chair in either committee called the paper of interest to few readers or suited to another venue; h7Rc's 'application paper' objection is about novelty, not breadth.
B, the accepting committee, had no low-scoring misreading detractor; A's misreading reviewer h7Rc sat in the rejecting committee.
A alone received BDD100K test and runtime results, but no A score rose; B's scores rose on the shared core rebuttal, not on results only B saw.
A's highest-confidence reviewer (x3ez, confidence 5) rated 5, not above the others; B's reviewers all had confidence 4.
No A review was edited after posting, and x3ez's 2021-08-29 comment was answered by the authors; no late unrebutted objection exists.
B's verbal assessments were more favourable (novelty found, 'a big step', concerns addressed) than A's ('pure application paper', 'trivial' gain), so the gap is not scoring leniency alone.

A's x3ez showed the efficiency claim holds for memory but not speed (63.2 vs 61.8 ms) and called the 0.5-0.6 AP gain trivial, a main reason for reject, while B's AC called the trade-off 'very strong'.
A's reviewers rated mostly 5 at confidence 3 to 5, below the marginal-accept rating, and B's flat 7s and 6 were at confidence 4 with no stated inability to check.
